headline: High-risk shared-workspace pair: Dify can write shared state while gpt-researcher reads/writes broad files and uses networked tools, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify has shared state via the Dify server datastore and can write files; gpt-researcher reads files, uses browsers, and can ingest local documents. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge even without a documented direct channel. The pathway is not provably blocked, but it is not clearly default-manual either.
conditions: IF Dify outputs are stored in shared datastore and later consumed by gpt-researcher as task input, injection is possible.
IF gpt-researcher parses retrieved documents or web content as instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer behavior.
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct workspaces.
Disable automatic ingestion of Dify-generated text into gpt-researcher prompts.
Add a human review step before passing outputs between agents.
Strip instructions from retrieved documents before reuse.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and instruction/content separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and read filesystem access, and Dify explicitly touches conversation logs and knowledge-base content while gpt-researcher handles local documents and reports. In a shared workspace, either agent can expose sensitive files or logs to external APIs by default. The blast radius includes multiple work products and sensitive content.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or mounted files, file contents can flow to external model/search APIs.
IF Dify conversation logs or knowledge-base files are reused by gpt-researcher, sensitive data may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Use separate directories and credentials for each agent.
Remove sensitive files from the shared workspace before running either agent.
Disable external API calls for tasks that do not require them.
Review outbound destinations for both agents before execution.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dify can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; gpt-researcher can also read/write through its file handling and spawn subprocesses, with both supporting multiple instances. The profiles do not show locking or coordination primitives, so concurrent writes to shared resources are plausible. Uncertainty about exact shared paths pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or mutable artifact, concurrent writes can clobber each other.
IF the orchestrator does not provide locking, race conditions can corrupt outputs.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate output directory.
Run the agents sequentially instead of concurrently.
Avoid shared mutable git or database state.
Check for file locks before writes.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking and conflict resolution.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify is an orchestration platform that can emit agent/workflow outputs, and gpt-researcher is a planner/execution/publisher pipeline that can treat upstream text as research input. If gpt-researcher consumes Dify output without verification, errors or hallucinations can propagate into reports or actions. The pair lacks an explicit verification boundary in the profiles.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher uses Dify output as authoritative input, upstream mistakes can be amplified.
IF publisher steps act on unverified research, incorrect claims can reach final deliverables.
mitigations: Insert a verification step between agents.
Require source citations before downstream use.
Compare outputs against original documents manually.
Limit publisher actions to draft-only mode.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking and confidence gating.

E_compliance.rationale: Dify explicitly handles conversation logs and knowledge-base content, while gpt-researcher handles local documents, citations, and reports. The profiles do not specify residency, retention, or certification alignment, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. Because uncertainty must escalate, medium is appropriate rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Dify conversation logs and then processed by gpt-researcher, retention or residency obligations may be violated.
IF the two agents have different logging policies, the same data class may be retained inconsistently.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs.
Review retention settings for both systems.
Delete logs after the task completes.
Confirm data residency before processing.
requires-engineering: document and enforce compliance boundaries per agent.
